short_excerpt: The driver of a vehicle may overtake and pass upon the right of another vehicle only under the following conditions:
condition_summary: The overtaken driver makes or signals a left turn.
Certain unobstructed, unoccupied roads have sufficient width for at least two moving lines per direction.
Other unmarked pavement and right-turn-lane cases have additional distance, intersection and private-way limits.
One-way roads provide a separate possible condition.
Every permitted right-side pass also requires conditions allowing the movement in safety under subsection 2.
source_role: Governing-rule citation for the NRS 484B.207(2) right-pass exception premise; each alternative still requires original road and maneuver facts.
